purpose: Derive how a lower Rs/Rm bound interacts with the explicit NPulseChannel update and inventory the time-scale range in current TimeLearnerMatrix Train inputs.

assumptions: One synapse contributes at most 1/Rs conductance (normalized presynaptic output is at most 1).
For N simultaneously connected equivalent synapses, the maximum G*R is N/rho.
R is the channel resistance selected by NPulseChannel::ACalculate2 for that update; the BR480 evidence uses R=RestingResistance=Resistance=10 Mohm.

When abs(membrane Feedback)>=1e-3, the same update switches to FBResistance; any general bound must calculate that branch separately. BR480 TimeConstant values match the ordinary R=10 Mohm branch, so its observed runaway did not use FBResistance.
K<=1 prevents crossing the instantaneous equilibrium in one update; 1<K<=2 changes the sign of the deviation from equilibrium; K>2 is linearly unstable for constant input.

br480_observation.interpretation: The observed active-synapse updates are far outside the stability range. This is consistent with alternating-sign runaway in the saved channel trace; the ratio floor is a plausible targeted guard, but no training result has yet validated a candidate floor.

matrix_input_inventory.scope_note: This recursive inventory includes historical and control inputs; 312 is not asserted to be the count of rows in the primary experiment manifest.

historical_config_outlier.interpretation: At Q=0.5, zero synaptic conductance is already at the explicit scheme's K=2 boundary; any positive G makes K>2. No finite Rs/Rm can ensure strict linear stability for this configured time step.

next_validation: Verify the maximum normalized synaptic conductance and effective synapse count on the target channel for PSI on/off.
Run a Release-only BR480 diagnostic on .17 with a candidate lower Rs/Rm floor around the derived threshold, then inspect Need, peak validity, channel potential extrema, and quality separately.
Check the minimum-Q case in the planned matrix; investigate Q=0.5 legacy inputs as a time-step/integration issue that an Rs floor cannot repair.
